parts.text: Suggest one reason why distillation is expensive for supplying a whole city such as Karachi.
parts.answer: Large amounts of energy/fuel are needed to boil the water.

parts.label: d
parts.text: As water distils off, the boiling temperature of the remaining seawater slowly rises. Suggest why.
parts.answer: The salt becomes more concentrated (more impurity).

practice.stem: A student uses paper chromatography to examine the dyes in a felt-tip pen.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why the starting line must be above the level of the solvent.
parts.answer: Otherwise the spots dissolve into the solvent in the beaker instead of moving up the paper.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why a lid is placed on the beaker.
parts.answer: To stop the solvent evaporating, so the paper stays saturated with vapour.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write the expression used to calculate an Rf value.
parts.answer: Rf = distance moved by spot ÷ distance moved by solvent (both measured from the starting line)

practice.stem:
A bank in Faisalabad suspects a cheque has been altered. Ink from the cheque and from three suspects' pens, P, Q and R, is run on the same chromatography paper. The solvent moves 8.0 cm from the starting line.
Cheque ink: spots at 2.4 cm and 5.6 cm
Pen P: spots at 2.4 cm and 4.0 cm
Pen Q: spots at 2.4 cm and 5.6 cm
Pen R: one spot at 5.6 cm

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the Rf value of each spot from the cheque ink.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Which pen, P, Q or R, was used to write on the cheque? Explain.
parts.answer: Q; it has two spots with the same Rf values (same distances) as the cheque ink.
parts.working: B1 Q; B1 both spots match.

parts.label: c
parts.text: How many dyes are in pen P?
parts.answer: Two

practice.stem: Two samples of amino acids, K and L, are separated by paper chromatography. After locating the spots, K shows one spot and L shows three spots.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Which substance is pure? Explain.
parts.answer: Substance K; it gives only one spot.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The amino acid spots are colourless. Describe how they are made visible.
parts.answer: Spray the dried paper with a locating agent.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State how many substances are present in L.
parts.answer: Three

practice.stem: In a chromatogram a dye spot moves 3.6 cm and the solvent front moves 8.0 cm from the starting line.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the Rf value of the dye.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why an Rf value can never be greater than 1.
parts.answer: A spot cannot move further than the solvent that carries it.

practice.stem:
Colours from three lipsticks bought in a market in Lahore are run on chromatography paper. Distances moved from the starting line are recorded.
Lipstick L: 3.0 cm, 6.5 cm
Lipstick M: 1.2 cm, 3.0 cm, 5.0 cm
Lipstick N: 3.0 cm

parts.label: a
parts.text: How many different dyes are in lipstick M?
parts.answer: Three

parts.label: b
parts.text: Which dye is present in all three lipsticks?
parts.answer: The dye at 3.0 cm

parts.label: c
parts.text: Lipstick N gives only one spot. What does this suggest?
parts.answer: It contains a single dye (possibly pure).

practice.stem:
A food inspector in Lahore tests the colouring from a sweet using paper chromatography. A spot of the colouring is placed on a pencil line 1.0 cm from the bottom of the paper. After the experiment, the solvent front is 8.0 cm above the starting line and two spots are seen, 2.4 cm and 5.6 cm above the starting line.
Rf values of permitted dyes in the same solvent: dye E 0.30, dye F 0.55, dye G 0.70, dye H 0.85.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why the starting line is drawn in pencil and not in ink.
parts.answer: Pencil (graphite) does not dissolve in the solvent and move up the paper; ink would.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the Rf values of the two spots.
parts.working: Rf = distance moved by spot ÷ distance moved by solvent M1; 2.4 ÷ 8.0 = 0.30, 5.6 ÷ 8.0 = 0.70 A1

parts.label: c
parts.text: Use the data to identify which permitted dyes are in the sweet colouring.
parts.answer: E and G

parts.label: d
parts.text: Suggest how the spots of a colourless substance could be seen on a chromatogram.
parts.answer: Spray with a locating agent (then dry/heat).

practice.stem:
A protein is hydrolysed and the products are run on chromatography paper, then sprayed with a locating agent. The solvent front moves 8.0 cm. Two spots appear at 2.1 cm and 4.8 cm from the starting line.
Rf values of amino acids in this solvent: glycine 0.26; alanine 0.38; valine 0.60; leucine 0.73

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the Rf values of the two spots from the hydrolysed protein.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Identify the two amino acids.
parts.answer: Glycine and valine

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the student should not touch the paper with her fingers.
parts.answer: Skin contains amino acids that would show up as extra spots.

practice.stem: A student runs a black ink in water as the solvent.

parts.label: a
parts.text: One dye stays on the starting line. State its Rf value and explain what this tells you.
parts.answer: 0; it is insoluble in this solvent.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Suggest how the student could find out whether this dye is a single substance.
parts.answer: Repeat the chromatography with a different solvent in which it dissolves.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Another dye moves with the solvent front. Explain why its Rf value is not useful for identifying it.
parts.answer: Rf = 1; it is very soluble and does not separate from other very soluble substances.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Plan an experiment to find out whether an orange drink contains a banned dye E. You are given the drink, a pure sample of dye E, chromatography paper, a solvent, a beaker with lid and a ruler.
parts.answer: Draw a pencil base line about 2 cm from the bottom; put a small concentrated spot of drink and a spot of dye E side by side on the line; stand the paper in solvent below the line, cover; remove when solvent is near the top, mark the solvent front; dry; if the drink has a spot at the same height/Rf as E, it contains E.
parts.working: 1 mark each for any five: pencil line; small spots of drink and of E on the line; solvent below line; lid; mark solvent front and dry; compare positions/Rf values.

practice.stem: A dye has an Rf value of 0.62 in a particular solvent. In an experiment the solvent front moves 9.5 cm from the starting line.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate how far the spot has moved from the starting line. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.
parts.working: M1 distance = Rf × solvent distance; A1 0.62 × 9.5 = 5.89 cm.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the position of the solvent front must be marked as soon as the paper is removed.
parts.answer: The solvent evaporates quickly and the front becomes invisible.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain how paper chromatography separates the dyes in a mixture.
parts.answer: Dyes have different solubilities in the solvent (and different attractions to the paper); more soluble dyes are carried further up the paper.
parts.working: B1 different solubility/attraction; B1 more soluble moves further.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the base line is drawn in pencil, not ink.
parts.answer: Pencil (graphite) is insoluble and does not move; ink would separate and confuse the result.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the spot of mixture is small and concentrated.
parts.answer: So the separated spots are distinct and do not overlap.

practice.stem: A student makes five mistakes when doing paper chromatography. Explain how each affects the result.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Mistake 1: the base line is drawn in ballpoint pen.
parts.answer: The ink of the line separates into spots, mixing with the sample spots.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Mistake 2: the base line is below the surface of the solvent.
parts.answer: The samples dissolve into the solvent and no chromatogram forms.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Mistake 3: the spots are large and placed touching each other.
parts.answer: Spots spread and merge, so dyes cannot be told apart.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Mistake 4: the solvent front is not marked and the paper is dried.
parts.answer: Rf values cannot be calculated.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Mistake 5: the paper touches the side of the beaker.
parts.answer: The solvent moves unevenly, giving a sloping front and wrong Rf values.

practice.stem:
Three food dyes are tested in two different solvents.
Rf in solvent 1: dye A 0.45; dye B 0.45; dye C 0.20
Rf in solvent 2: dye A 0.30; dye B 0.72; dye C 0.55
A single-dye sample S gives Rf 0.45 in solvent 1 and Rf 0.72 in solvent 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why solvent 1 alone cannot identify the dye in sample S.
parts.answer: Dyes A and B have the same Rf (0.45) in solvent 1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Identify the dye in S. Explain.
parts.answer: Dye B; its Rf in solvent 2 (0.72) matches S (0.72) and it matches in solvent 1 too.
parts.working: B1 B; B1 explanation using both solvents.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Sample T gives two spots in solvent 2 at Rf 0.30 and 0.72. Suggest which dyes it contains.
parts.answer: A and B

practice.stem:
On a chromatogram, all distances are measured from the bottom edge of the paper.
Starting line: 1.5 cm
Centre of spot: 6.2 cm
Solvent front: 11.0 cm

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the Rf value of the spot. Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 distances from base line: 6.2 − 1.5 = 4.7 cm and 11.0 − 1.5 = 9.5 cm; A1 4.7 ÷ 9.5 = 0.49.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Another student calculates 6.2 ÷ 11.0 = 0.56. Explain the error.
parts.answer: She measured from the bottom of the paper, not from the starting line.

practice.stem: A food laboratory checks whether a jar of honey sold in a market has had cheap sucrose syrup added. Samples are run by paper chromatography.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why a locating agent is needed in this experiment.
parts.answer: The sugars are colourless.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The honey gives spots at Rf 0.25 and 0.40; pure glucose gives Rf 0.25, fructose 0.40 and sucrose 0.15 under the same conditions. Deduce what the results show about the honey.
parts.answer: It contains glucose and fructose but no sucrose.
parts.working: B1 glucose and fructose; B1 no sucrose.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the pure sugars must be run on the same paper at the same time as the honey.
parts.answer: Rf values depend on solvent, paper and temperature; running together ensures identical conditions for comparison.
parts.working: B1 Rf depends on conditions; B1 fair comparison.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which statement about addition polymerisation is correct?
A The polymer is the only product.
B Water is given off as each link forms.
C The monomers must contain two different functional groups.
D The monomers are saturated.
parts.answer: A The polymer is the only product.
parts.working: In addition polymerisation unsaturated monomers (C=C) join and nothing else is produced. B describes condensation polymerisation.

parts.label: a
parts.text: PVC is made from chloroethene, CH₂=CHCl. Name the type of polymerisation.
parts.answer: addition

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the repeat unit of PVC.
parts.answer: –CH₂–CHCl– (shown in brackets with continuation bonds, n outside)
parts.working: B1 single C–C backbone; B1 correct atoms and continuation bonds.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give one use of PVC.
parts.answer: water pipes / insulation for electrical cables / window frames

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the monomer used to make poly(ethene) and give its formula.
parts.answer: ethene, CH₂=CH₂ (C₂H₄)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write an equation for the polymerisation, using n for the number of monomer molecules.
parts.answer: n CH₂=CH₂ → –(CH₂–CH₂)ₙ–
parts.working: B1 n monomers; B1 repeat unit in brackets with n.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give two uses of poly(ethene).
parts.answer: Any two: plastic bags; cling film; bottles; buckets; washing-up bowls; insulation for wires.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give two differences between addition polymerisation and condensation polymerisation.
parts.answer: Addition: one product only (the polymer); monomers have a C=C bond. Condensation: a small molecule such as water is also formed; monomers have two functional groups (often two different monomers).

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the type of polymerisation used to make (i) PVC and (ii) nylon.
parts.answer: (i) addition (ii) condensation

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the type of natural polymer made from amino acids.
parts.answer: protein

parts.label: b
parts.text: The general structure of an amino acid is H₂N–CHR–COOH. Name the two functional groups.
parts.answer: amine (–NH₂) and carboxylic acid (–COOH)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the type of polymerisation that joins amino acids and the linkage formed.
parts.answer: condensation; amide (peptide) linkage

practice.stem: A city council plans to ban single-use plastic shopping bags.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why disposing of plastics in landfill sites causes problems.
parts.answer: Most plastics are non-biodegradable, so they remain for a very long time and take up land.
parts.working: B1 non-biodegradable; B1 persist / use up space.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe one problem caused by plastic waste in rivers and seas.
parts.answer: Harms or kills marine animals that swallow it or become trapped; microplastics enter food chains; blocks drains.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Burning plastic waste is sometimes suggested. Give one disadvantage.
parts.answer: Produces toxic gases (e.g. hydrogen chloride from PVC, carbon monoxide) / releases carbon dioxide.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Suggest one way a city council could reduce plastic waste.
parts.answer: Ban or charge for single-use plastic bags; encourage recycling or reusable bags.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Nylon is a polyamide. Name the two types of monomer used to make it and the linkage formed.
parts.answer: a dicarboxylic acid and a diamine; amide linkage, –CONH–
parts.working: B1 dicarboxylic acid; B1 diamine; B1 amide linkage.

parts.label: b
parts.text: PET is a polyester. Name the two types of monomer and the linkage.
parts.answer: a dicarboxylic acid and a diol; ester linkage, –COO–

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the small molecule formed when each linkage is made, and the type of polymerisation.
parts.answer: water; condensation polymerisation

parts.label: a
parts.text:
A polymer has the repeat unit –CH₂–CH(CN)–. What is the formula of its monomer?
A CH₂=CHCN
B CH₃CH₂CN
C CH₂=C(CN)₂
D CH₃CH(CN)₂
parts.answer: A CH₂=CHCN
parts.working: In addition polymerisation the C=C of the monomer opens to form the two-carbon repeat unit, so the monomer is CH₂=CHCN. B and D are saturated and cannot polymerise by addition; C has two CN groups, which the repeat unit does not.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Polystyrene has the repeat unit –CH₂–CH(C₆H₅)–. Give the structural formula of its monomer.
parts.answer: CH₂=CH(C₆H₅) (CH₂=CHC₆H₅)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Poly(propene) is made from propene, CH₂=CHCH₃. Write the repeat unit of poly(propene).
parts.answer: –CH₂–CH(CH₃)–

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the empirical formula of poly(propene) is the same as that of propene.
parts.answer: The polymer is made only by joining propene molecules with no other product, so the ratio of C to H atoms (CH₂) is unchanged.
parts.working: B1 addition – no atoms lost; B1 same C:H ratio CH₂.

practice.stem: A school in Islamabad starts a project to collect used plastic drinks bottles for recycling.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain what is meant by 'non-biodegradable'.
parts.answer: It is not broken down by microorganisms/bacteria in the environment.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give two advantages of recycling plastic bottles rather than putting them in landfill.
parts.answer: Any two: saves petroleum (a finite resource); reduces landfill space; less litter/harm to wildlife; uses less energy than making new plastic.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest why different types of plastic must be sorted before recycling.
parts.answer: Different polymers have different properties/melting points, so a mixture gives a poor-quality product.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Proteins are natural polymers. Name the monomers and the linkage in proteins.
parts.answer: amino acids; amide (peptide) linkage

parts.label: b
parts.text: A protein chain is made from 50 amino acid molecules joined in a line. How many water molecules are eliminated?
parts.working: B1 one water molecule per linkage; 50 − 1 = 49 linkages.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give one similarity and one difference between the structures of a protein and nylon.
parts.answer: Similarity: both contain amide linkages / both condensation polymers. Difference: a protein is made from many different amino acids (each monomer has both –NH₂ and –COOH groups), whereas nylon is made from two different monomers that alternate.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the repeat unit of poly(propene), made from propene CH₂=CHCH₃.
parts.answer: –CH₂–CH(CH₃)–
parts.working: B1 two-carbon backbone with continuation bonds; B1 CH₃ as a side group.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A poly(propene) molecule is made from 5000 propene molecules. Calculate its relative molecular mass. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1)

parts.label: c
parts.text: The repeat unit of a non-stick coating is –CF₂–CF₂–. Give the structural formula and name of its monomer.
parts.answer: CF₂=CF₂; tetrafluoroethene

practice.stem:
Nylon is made from the diamine H₂N–(CH₂)₆–NH₂ and the dicarboxylic acid HOOC–(CH₂)₄–COOH.
[Ar: H, 1; C, 12; N, 14; O, 16]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the linkage formed between the monomers.
parts.answer: amide linkage, –CONH–

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the small molecule eliminated each time a linkage forms.
parts.answer: water

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write the molecular formula of the repeat unit –NH–(CH₂)₆–NH–CO–(CH₂)₄–CO– and calculate its relative formula mass.
parts.answer: C₁₂H₂₂N₂O₂; 226

parts.label: d
parts.text: A single chain is made from 150 diamine molecules and 150 dicarboxylic acid molecules joined alternately. How many water molecules are eliminated?
parts.working: 300 monomers in a line form 299 links, one water molecule per link.

practice.stem:
PVC is made from chloroethene, CH₂=CHCl.
[Ar: H, 1; C, 12; Cl, 35.5]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the relative formula mass of the repeat unit –CH₂–CHCl–.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A sample of PVC has an average relative molecular mass of 125 000. Calculate the average number of monomer units in one chain.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the percentage by mass of chlorine in PVC, to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Explain why burning PVC waste produces an acidic gas and name the gas.
parts.answer: PVC contains chlorine, which forms hydrogen chloride when it burns; HCl dissolves in water to give an acidic solution.
parts.working: B1 hydrogen chloride; B1 from Cl in polymer.

practice.stem:
Sections of three polymer chains are shown.
P: –CH₂–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–
Q: –O–CH₂CH₂–O–CO–C₆H₄–CO–O–CH₂CH₂–O–
R: –NH–CH(CH₃)–CO–NH–CH₂–CO–NH–CH(CH₃)–CO–

parts.label: a
parts.text: For each section, state the type of polymerisation.
parts.answer: P addition; Q condensation; R condensation

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the linkage in Q and in R.
parts.answer: Q ester linkage; R amide linkage

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the two types of monomer used to make Q.
parts.answer: a diol and a dicarboxylic acid

parts.label: d
parts.text: R comes from a natural polymer. Name the type of natural polymer.
parts.answer: protein

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which ester is formed when methanol reacts with ethanoic acid?
A ethyl methanoate
B methyl ethanoate
C methyl methanoate
D ethyl ethanoate
parts.answer: B methyl ethanoate
parts.working: The alcohol gives the first part of the name (methyl) and the acid gives the second part (ethanoate). A reverses the two parts.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Vinegar contains ethanoic acid. Write a balanced equation for the reaction of ethanoic acid with sodium carbonate, and give one observation.
parts.answer: 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂; effervescence (bubbles)
parts.working: B1 formulae; B1 balanced; B1 observation.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the salt formed when ethanoic acid reacts with magnesium, and name the gas.
parts.answer: magnesium ethanoate; hydrogen

parts.label: c
parts.text: Ethanoic acid is a weak acid. Explain what this means.
parts.answer: It is only partially dissociated (ionised) in water.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
What is the structural formula of propanoic acid?
A CH₃CH₂COOH
B CH₃CH₂CH₂OH
C CH₃COOCH₃
D CH₃COOH
parts.answer: A CH₃CH₂COOH
parts.working: Propanoic acid has three carbon atoms including the –COOH carbon. B is propan-1-ol (an alcohol); C is methyl ethanoate (an ester); D is ethanoic acid (two carbons).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the reagent used to oxidise ethanol to ethanoic acid in the laboratory, and state the colour change.
parts.answer: Acidified potassium manganate(VII); purple to colourless.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the process by which ethanoic acid forms when wine or fruit juice is left open to the air.
parts.answer: Bacterial oxidation (of ethanol)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the functional group in ethanoic acid.
parts.answer: carboxylic acid group, –COOH

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why vinegar can be used to remove limescale (calcium carbonate) from a tap.
parts.answer: Vinegar contains ethanoic acid, which reacts with carbonates (forming a soluble salt).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the gas given off.
parts.answer: carbon dioxide

parts.label: c
parts.text: Is ethanoic acid a strong or a weak acid? Suggest a pH for vinegar.
parts.answer: weak acid; pH about 3 (2–4)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the ester formed when ethanol reacts with propanoic acid and write its structural formula.
parts.answer: ethyl propanoate; CH₃CH₂COOCH₂CH₃

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the conditions for this reaction.
parts.answer: concentrated sulfuric acid (catalyst); heat (warm)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give one use of esters.
parts.answer: flavourings / perfumes / solvents

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the carboxylic acid and the alcohol that react to make propyl methanoate, HCOOCH₂CH₂CH₃.
parts.answer: methanoic acid; propan-1-ol

parts.label: b
parts.text: Ethyl butanoate, CH₃CH₂CH₂COOCH₂CH₃, has a pineapple smell. Name the acid and alcohol used to make it.
parts.answer: butanoic acid; ethanol

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write the molecular formula of ethyl butanoate and calculate its relative molecular mass. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
parts.answer: C₆H₁₂O₂; 116

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Name the esters:
(i) CH₃CH₂COOCH₃
(ii) HCOOCH₂CH₃
(iii) CH₃COOCH₂CH₂CH₂CH₃
parts.answer: (i) methyl propanoate (ii) ethyl methanoate (iii) butyl ethanoate

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the acid and alcohol needed to make ester (iii).
parts.answer: ethanoic acid and butan-1-ol (butanol)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a balanced equation for the reaction of ethanoic acid with aqueous potassium hydroxide, and name the salt.
parts.answer: CH₃COOH + KOH → CH₃COOK + H₂O; potassium ethanoate

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write a balanced equation for the reaction of ethanoic acid with calcium carbonate.
parts.answer: 2CH₃COOH + CaCO₃ → (CH₃COO)₂Ca + H₂O + CO₂

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why this reaction is slower than the reaction of calcium carbonate with hydrochloric acid of the same concentration.
parts.answer: Ethanoic acid is weak/partially ionised, so it has a lower concentration of H⁺ ions.

practice.stem: A student warms a mixture of ethanol, ethanoic acid and a few drops of concentrated sulfuric acid in a test-tube placed in a beaker of hot water for 5 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why the mixture is heated in a water bath and not over a Bunsen flame.
parts.answer: Ethanol is flammable / has a low boiling point.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the purpose of the concentrated sulfuric acid.
parts.answer: catalyst

parts.label: c
parts.text: After heating, the mixture is poured into aqueous sodium carbonate. Describe two observations.
parts.answer: Effervescence (from unreacted acid); a sweet/fruity smell; an oily layer floating on the surface.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Name the ester formed.
parts.answer: ethyl ethanoate

practice.stem:
A student titrates 25.0 cm³ of a vinegar sample from a shop in Multan with 1.00 mol/dm³ sodium hydroxide. The mean titre is 20.8 cm³.
CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of sodium hydroxide used.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the concentration of ethanoic acid in the vinegar in mol/dm³.
parts.answer: 0.832 mol/dm³

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the concentration in g/dm³ to 3 significant figures. (Mr CH₃COOH = 60)
parts.answer: 49.9 g/dm³

parts.label: d
parts.text: Name a suitable indicator and give the colour change at the end-point.
parts.answer: Thymolphthalein: colourless to blue (accept phenolphthalein: colourless to pink).
parts.working: B1 indicator suitable for a weak acid–strong base titration (thymolphthalein or phenolphthalein; not methyl orange); B1 matching colour change at the end-point.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction of ethanoic acid with ethanol.
parts.answer: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O

parts.label: b
parts.text: 6.0 g of ethanoic acid reacts with excess ethanol. Calculate the maximum mass of ethyl ethanoate. (Mr: CH₃COOH = 60, CH₃COOC₂H₅ = 88)

parts.label: c
parts.text: The student obtains 5.72 g. Calculate the percentage yield.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Give two reasons why the yield is less than 100 %.
parts.answer: The reaction is reversible / reaches equilibrium; some product lost during separation or purification; some ester evaporates (volatile).

practice.stem:
A student heats 7.40 g of propanoic acid with excess methanol and a few drops of concentrated sulfuric acid.
[Mr: propanoic acid = 74; methyl propanoate = 88]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction, using structural formulae.
parts.answer: CH₃CH₂COOH + CH₃OH ⇌ CH₃CH₂COOCH₃ + H₂O
parts.working: B1 ester; B1 water and balanced.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the maximum mass of methyl propanoate that can be formed.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The student obtains 6.16 g. Calculate the percentage yield.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Write the molecular formula and the empirical formula of methyl propanoate.
parts.answer: C₄H₈O₂; C₂H₄O

practice.stem:
0.444 g of a monobasic carboxylic acid is dissolved in water and titrated with 0.300 mol/dm³ aqueous sodium hydroxide. 20.0 cm³ is needed.
RCOOH + NaOH → RCOONa + H₂O
[Ar: H, 1; C, 12; O, 16]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of sodium hydroxide used.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the relative molecular mass of the acid.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The acid has the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH. Deduce its formula and name.
parts.answer: C₂H₅COOH; propanoic acid

practice.stem: Liquid X has the molecular formula C₃H₆O₂. It is either propanoic acid or methyl ethanoate.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the structural formulae of propanoic acid and methyl ethanoate.
parts.answer: CH₃CH₂COOH; CH₃COOCH₃

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why these two compounds are structural isomers.
parts.answer: Same molecular formula (C₃H₆O₂) but different structural formulae.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Describe a chemical test to show which compound X is. Give the result for each compound.
parts.answer: Add sodium carbonate (or magnesium); propanoic acid fizzes (CO₂ / H₂); methyl ethanoate gives no fizzing.
parts.working: B1 reagent and acid result; B1 ester no reaction.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Name one other ester with the molecular formula C₃H₆O₂.
parts.answer: ethyl methanoate

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which compound is in the same homologous series as ethanol?
A C₃H₇OH
B CH₃COOH
C C₃H₆
D C₂H₆
parts.answer: A C₃H₇OH
parts.working: C₃H₇OH (propanol) has the same –OH functional group and general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH. CH₃COOH (B) is a carboxylic acid, a different series.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give three characteristics of a homologous series.
parts.answer: Same general formula; same functional group; similar chemical properties; a trend in physical properties (e.g. boiling point increases with chain length); each member differs from the next by CH₂.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The general formula of the alkanes is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Write the molecular formula of the alkane with 8 carbon atoms, found in petrol.
parts.answer: C₈H₁₈

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write the general formula of the alkenes.
parts.answer: CₙH₂ₙ

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Name these compounds:
(i) CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃
(ii) CH₃OH
(iii) CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃
(iv) HCOOH
parts.answer: (i) butane (ii) methanol (iii) but-1-ene (iv) methanoic acid

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what is meant by a functional group.
parts.answer: An atom or group of atoms that determines the chemical properties of a homologous series.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give the functional group of: (i) alcohols (ii) alkenes (iii) carboxylic acids (iv) esters
parts.answer: (i) –OH (ii) C=C (iii) –COOH (iv) –COO–

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Complete the general formula and the name of the first member for each homologous series:
(i) alkanes (ii) alkenes (iii) alcohols (iv) carboxylic acids
parts.answer: (i) CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, methane (ii) CₙH₂ₙ, ethene (iii) CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH, methanol (iv) CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH, methanoic acid

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Name these compounds:
(i) CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂OH
(ii) CH₃CH=CHCH₃
(iii) CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH
parts.answer: (i) pentan-1-ol (ii) but-2-ene (iii) butanoic acid

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain what the number in the name but-2-ene tells you.
parts.answer: The C=C double bond starts at carbon atom 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what is meant by structural isomers.
parts.answer: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae.
parts.working: B1 same molecular formula; B1 different structures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the structural formulae of the two structural isomers with the molecular formula C₄H₁₀.
parts.answer: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ (butane) and CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₃ (methylpropane)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write the structural formulae of but-1-ene and but-2-ene.
parts.answer: but-1-ene: CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃; but-2-ene: CH₃CH=CHCH₃

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Name each compound:
(i) CH₃CH₂COOH
(ii) CH₃CH₂CH₂OH
(iii) CH₃CH=CH₂
(iv) CH₃COOCH₂CH₃
parts.answer: (i) propanoic acid (ii) propan-1-ol (iii) propene (iv) ethyl ethanoate

parts.label: b
parts.text: Identify the functional group in compounds (i) and (iii).
parts.answer: (i) carboxylic acid group, –COOH; (iii) carbon–carbon double bond, C=C

parts.label: a
parts.text:
How many structural isomers have the molecular formula C₅H₁₂?
A 2
B 3
C 4
D 5
parts.answer: B 3
parts.working: Pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane. A common error is to count only straight and singly-branched chains (2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: For propan-1-ol, give (i) the molecular formula and (ii) the structural formula.
parts.answer: (i) C₃H₈O (ii) CH₃CH₂CH₂OH

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give the empirical formula of (i) ethene, C₂H₄, (ii) hex-1-ene, C₆H₁₂ and (iii) butane, C₄H₁₀.
parts.answer: (i) CH₂ (ii) CH₂ (iii) C₂H₅

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why all alkenes have the same empirical formula.
parts.answer: The general formula is CₙH₂ₙ, so the C : H ratio is always 1 : 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the structural formulae of pent-1-ene and pent-2-ene.
parts.answer: CH₂=CHCH₂CH₂CH₃; CH₃CH=CHCH₂CH₃

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why they are structural isomers.
parts.answer: Same molecular formula (C₅H₁₀), different position of the C=C bond.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest why both compounds decolourise aqueous bromine.
parts.answer: Both contain a C=C double bond (same functional group).

parts.label: a
parts.text: An alkene has a relative molecular mass of 56. Deduce its molecular formula. Show your working. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1)
parts.answer: C₄H₈

parts.label: b
parts.text: Draw (as structural formulae) two alkenes with this molecular formula and name them.
parts.answer: CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃ but-1-ene; CH₃CH=CHCH₃ but-2-ene (also CH₂=C(CH₃)CH₃, methylpropene)
parts.working: B1 each correct formula with name.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The molecular formula C₃H₈O fits two alcohols. Give their structural formulae and names.
parts.answer: CH₃CH₂CH₂OH propan-1-ol; CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ propan-2-ol

practice.stem:
Boiling points of the first five alkanes:
alkane | methane | ethane | propane | butane | pentane
boiling point / °C | −162 | −89 | −42 | −1 | 36

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe the trend in boiling point.
parts.answer: Boiling point increases as the number of carbon atoms increases.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Predict the boiling point of hexane, C₆H₁₄.
parts.answer: about 69 °C (accept 60–75 °C)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain the trend.
parts.answer: Molecules get larger, so the forces of attraction between molecules (intermolecular forces) get stronger and more energy is needed to separate them.
parts.working: B1 larger molecules; B1 stronger intermolecular forces.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Which of these alkanes are gases at 25 °C?
parts.answer: methane, ethane, propane and butane

parts.label: e
parts.text: State one way in which members of a homologous series are similar.
parts.answer: Same general formula / same functional group / similar chemical properties / differ by CH₂.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A carboxylic acid has a relative molecular mass of 88. Use the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH to find its molecular formula and name it. Show your working.
parts.answer: C₃H₇COOH (C₄H₈O₂); butanoic acid
parts.working: M1 14n + 46 = 88; M1 n = 3; A1 formula and name.

parts.label: b
parts.text: An ester has the same molecular formula. Give its name and structural formula.
parts.answer: ethyl ethanoate, CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ (or methyl propanoate CH₃CH₂COOCH₃ / propyl methanoate HCOOCH₂CH₂CH₃)

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the name given to compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae.
parts.answer: structural isomers

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Sort these formulae into homologous series (alkane, alkene, alcohol, carboxylic acid):
C₆H₁₄, C₇H₁₄, C₄H₉OH, C₅H₁₁COOH, C₉H₂₀
parts.answer: alkanes C₆H₁₄ and C₉H₂₀; alkene C₇H₁₄; alcohol C₄H₉OH; carboxylic acid C₅H₁₁COOH
parts.working: B3 all correct; B2 four; B1 three.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the molecular formula of the alkane with 10 carbon atoms and calculate its relative molecular mass.
parts.answer: C₁₀H₂₂; 142

parts.label: c
parts.text: By how much does the relative molecular mass increase from one member of a homologous series to the next?
parts.answer: 14 (one CH₂ group)

practice.stem: Several sugar mills in Pakistan also produce ethanol from molasses.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Ethanol can be made by fermentation of sugar from sugar cane molasses. State the conditions needed.
parts.answer: Yeast; temperature about 25–35 °C; absence of oxygen (anaerobic); aqueous solution.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the equation for the fermentation of glucose.
parts.answer: C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the other industrial method of making ethanol.
parts.answer: Catalytic addition of steam to ethene (hydration of ethene).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give two uses of ethanol.
parts.answer: As a solvent; as a fuel.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write a balanced equation for the complete combustion of ethanol.
parts.answer: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the names and structural formulae of the first three alcohols with an –OH group at the end of the chain.
parts.answer: methanol CH₃OH; ethanol CH₃CH₂OH; propan-1-ol CH₃CH₂CH₂OH

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the general formula of the alcohols.
parts.answer: CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH

practice.stem: Some countries add ethanol to petrol to make a fuel called E10 (10 % ethanol).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why ethanol made from sugar cane is described as a renewable fuel.
parts.answer: Sugar cane can be regrown each year (it is not used up like fossil fuels).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the products of the complete combustion of ethanol.
parts.answer: carbon dioxide and water

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give one use of ethanol other than as a fuel.
parts.answer: solvent (e.g. in perfumes, medicines, hand sanitiser)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the structural formula and the molecular formula of propan-1-ol.
parts.answer: CH₃CH₂CH₂OH; C₃H₈O

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the relative molecular mass of propan-1-ol. [Ar: H, 1; C, 12; O, 16]

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the homologous series to which propan-1-ol belongs.
parts.answer: alcohols

parts.label: a
parts.text: State two physical properties of ethanol.
parts.answer: Any two: colourless liquid; mixes completely with water; volatile / low boiling point (78 °C); characteristic smell.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hand sanitiser gel contains ethanol. Suggest one safety precaution when using it.
parts.answer: Keep away from flames – ethanol is flammable.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the two main industrial methods of making ethanol.
parts.answer: fermentation (of glucose/sugar) and catalytic addition of steam to ethene

parts.label: a
parts.text: Compare making ethanol by fermentation with making it by the catalytic addition of steam to ethene. Give two advantages of each method.
parts.answer: Fermentation: uses renewable raw materials (sugar crops); low temperature and normal pressure so less energy. Hydration of ethene: fast reaction; continuous process; produces pure ethanol (no need for separation); high yield.
parts.working: B1 each of two fermentation advantages; B1 each of two hydration advantages.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Suggest why a country with a large sugar industry and little petroleum might choose fermentation.
parts.answer: Sugar (molasses) is readily available and cheap, while ethene comes from petroleum, which would have to be imported.

practice.stem: Most industrial ethanol in oil-producing countries is made by the catalytic addition of steam to ethene.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction of ethene with steam.
parts.answer: C₂H₄ + H₂O → C₂H₅OH

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the conditions used: temperature, pressure and catalyst.
parts.answer: about 300 °C; about 6000 kPa (60 atm); phosphoric acid catalyst

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the type of reaction.
parts.answer: addition (hydration)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the structural formula of ethanol.
parts.answer: CH₃CH₂OH

parts.label: b
parts.text: Ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid. Write a balanced equation for this reaction, using [O] to represent the oxidising agent.
parts.answer: CH₃CH₂OH + 2[O] → CH₃COOH + H₂O
parts.working: B1 ethanol and ethanoic acid with the correct formulae; B1 balanced with 2[O] and water.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a balanced equation for the complete combustion of methanol, CH₃OH.
parts.answer: 2CH₃OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 4H₂O

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write a balanced equation for the complete combustion of propan-1-ol, C₃H₇OH.
parts.answer: 2C₃H₇OH + 9O₂ → 6CO₂ + 8H₂O

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the toxic gas formed if propan-1-ol burns in a limited supply of air.
parts.answer: carbon monoxide

practice.stem: [Mr: C₂H₅OH = 46. One mole of gas occupies 24 dm³ at r.t.p.]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the balanced equation for the complete combustion of ethanol.
parts.answer: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the volume of carbon dioxide, in dm³ at r.t.p., produced when 9.2 g of ethanol burns completely.
parts.answer: 9.6 dm³

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the volume of oxygen, in dm³ at r.t.p., needed.
parts.answer: 14.4 dm³

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the maximum mass of ethanol from 90 g of glucose. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
parts.working: M1 moles glucose = 90 ÷ 180 = 0.50, moles ethanol = 1.0; A1 1.0 × 46 = 46 g.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the volume of carbon dioxide produced at room temperature and pressure. (Molar gas volume = 24 dm³)
parts.answer: 24 dm³

parts.label: c
parts.text: Ethanol can be oxidised to ethanoic acid by warming with acidified aqueous potassium manganate(VII). State the colour change.
parts.answer: purple to colourless

practice.stem:
Yeast is added to glucose solution in a flask kept at 30 °C. The carbon dioxide produced each day is collected and measured at r.t.p.
Day | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6
Volume of CO₂ / cm³ | 40 | 95 | 120 | 80 | 30 | 5
[Mr: C₂H₅OH = 46. One mole of gas occupies 24 000 cm³ at r.t.p.]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the total volume of carbon dioxide collected.
parts.answer: 370 cm³

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the mass of ethanol produced, to 3 significant figures. (C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest why the rate of gas production falls after day 3.
parts.answer: The glucose is being used up; ethanol concentration rises and starts to kill/inhibit the yeast.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Explain why the flask is fitted with an air lock that lets gas out but no air in.
parts.answer: Fermentation needs anaerobic conditions; air (oxygen) would let ethanol be oxidised to ethanoic acid (or the yeast respire aerobically).

parts.label: e
parts.text: Name the method used to obtain a concentrated sample of ethanol from the mixture.
parts.answer: fractional distillation

practice.stem:
A spirit burner containing ethanol heats 200 g of water in a copper can. The temperature of the water rises by 30.0 °C, and 1.15 g of ethanol is burned.
[Mr: C₂H₅OH = 46]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the energy transferred to the water, in J. (Specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J/g/°C)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of ethanol burned.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the energy released per mole of ethanol, in kJ/mol.

parts.label: d
parts.text: The accepted value is about 1370 kJ/mol. Give two reasons for the difference.
parts.answer: Any two: heat lost to the surroundings/air; heat absorbed by the can; incomplete combustion (soot); evaporation of ethanol from the wick.

practice.stem:
Ethanol is made industrially by C₂H₄ + H₂O → C₂H₅OH.
[Mr: C₂H₄ = 28; C₂H₅OH = 46. 1 tonne = 10⁶ g]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the maximum mass of ethanol, in tonnes, that can be made from 1.4 tonnes of ethene.
parts.answer: 2.3 tonnes

parts.label: b
parts.text: Only about 5 % of the ethene is converted each time the gases pass over the catalyst. Explain how the plant still achieves an overall conversion of about 95 %.
parts.answer: The ethanol is condensed and removed; unreacted ethene is recycled back over the catalyst again and again.
parts.working: B1 remove product; B1 recycle unreacted ethene.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give one advantage of making ethanol from ethene rather than by fermentation.
parts.answer: Faster / continuous process / purer product (no distillation from dilute mixture needed).

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which test shows that a hydrocarbon is unsaturated?
A Aqueous bromine changes from orange to colourless.
B Limewater turns milky.
C Damp red litmus paper turns blue.
D A lighted splint gives a squeaky pop.
parts.answer: A Aqueous bromine changes from orange to colourless.
parts.working: C=C bonds undergo addition with bromine, decolourising it. B tests for carbon dioxide, which forms when any hydrocarbon burns, so it does not show unsaturation.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Which compound decolourises aqueous bromine at room temperature?
A ethane
B pentane
C but-2-ene
D methane
parts.answer: C but-2-ene
parts.working: But-2-ene is an alkene; its C=C bond undergoes addition with bromine. The others are alkanes (saturated) and do not react with aqueous bromine at room temperature.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the general formula of the alkenes.
parts.answer: CₙH₂ₙ

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain the meaning of the term unsaturated.
parts.answer: The molecule contains a carbon–carbon double bond (C=C).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write the molecular formula of the alkene with five carbon atoms.
parts.answer: C₅H₁₀

practice.stem: A student has two colourless liquids, hexane and hex-1-ene, in unlabelled bottles.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe a test that the student can use to identify the hex-1-ene.
parts.answer: Shake each with aqueous bromine; hex-1-ene turns it from orange (brown) to colourless.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the result with hexane.
parts.answer: Stays orange (no change).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the type of reaction between hex-1-ene and bromine.
parts.answer: addition

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a balanced equation for the complete combustion of ethene.
parts.answer: C₂H₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 2H₂O

parts.label: b
parts.text: Suggest why ethene is not used as a fuel, even though it burns well.
parts.answer: It is more valuable for making polymers and other chemicals.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the alkene used to make poly(propene).
parts.answer: propene

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the structural formula of this alkene.
parts.answer: CH₂=CHCH₃

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the homologous series to which it belongs and state its functional group.
parts.answer: alkenes; C=C

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Give the product and conditions for each reaction of ethene:
(i) with hydrogen
(ii) with steam
(iii) with bromine
parts.answer: (i) ethane; nickel catalyst, about 150 °C (ii) ethanol; phosphoric acid catalyst, about 300 °C and 6000 kPa (iii) 1,2-dibromoethane; room temperature
parts.working: (i) B1 ethane, B1 nickel catalyst + heat; (ii) B1 ethanol, B1 H₃PO₄ catalyst with high temperature and pressure; (iii) B1 1,2-dibromoethane (C₂H₄Br₂).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the type of reaction in all three cases.
parts.answer: addition

practice.stem: Banaspati ghee is made in Pakistan by hydrogenating unsaturated vegetable oils.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the gas that reacts with the unsaturated vegetable oil.
parts.answer: hydrogen

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the conditions used.
parts.answer: nickel catalyst; about 150 °C (heat)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why hydrogenation turns the liquid oil into a soft solid.
parts.answer: Hydrogen adds across C=C bonds, so the molecules become (more) saturated; this raises the melting point.
parts.working: B1 addition across C=C / saturated; B1 higher melting point.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Describe a test to show whether the product is still partly unsaturated.
parts.answer: Shake with aqueous bromine: decolourised if C=C bonds remain.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give the name of the product when but-1-ene reacts with (i) hydrogen and (ii) bromine.
parts.answer: (i) butane (ii) 1,2-dibromobutane

parts.label: b
parts.text: But-1-ene reacts with steam to form an alcohol. Give the molecular formula of the alcohol.
parts.answer: C₄H₉OH (C₄H₁₀O)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction of but-1-ene with bromine, using structural formulae.
parts.answer: CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃ + Br₂ → CH₂BrCHBrCH₂CH₃

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why alkenes are more reactive than alkanes.
parts.answer: Alkenes have a C=C double bond, which can open up for addition reactions; alkanes have only single bonds.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the process used in a refinery to make ethene from long-chain alkanes.
parts.answer: cracking

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give two important industrial uses of ethene.
parts.answer: Making poly(ethene); making ethanol (by hydration).

practice.stem:
A student tests three hydrocarbon liquids.
Liquid | effect of shaking with bromine water | appearance of flame when a few drops are burned
P | stays orange | yellow, slightly smoky
Q | orange to colourless | yellow, smoky
R | stays orange | yellow, very smoky (lots of soot)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Identify which liquid is an alkene. Explain.
parts.answer: Q; it decolourises bromine water, showing a C=C bond.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Suggest why liquid R burns with the smokiest flame.
parts.answer: R probably has more carbon in its molecules than P, so combustion is more incomplete and forms more soot.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State one safety precaution needed when burning these liquids.
parts.answer: Burn only small amounts on a heat-resistant mat, away from the stock bottles / wear eye protection / in a fume cupboard.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction of propene with bromine, using structural formulae, and name the product.
parts.answer: CH₃CH=CH₂ + Br₂ → CH₃CHBrCH₂Br; 1,2-dibromopropane

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the mass of bromine that reacts with 2.1 g of propene. (Ar: C = 12, H = 1, Br = 80)
parts.working: M1 Mr propene = 42, moles = 0.050; M1 1 : 1 ratio; A1 0.050 × 160 = 8.0 g.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why propane does not react with bromine in the dark.
parts.answer: Propane is saturated (no C=C), so it cannot undergo addition.

practice.stem:
0.70 g of an alkene reacts exactly with 1.60 g of bromine.
[Ar: H, 1; C, 12; Br, 80]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of bromine, Br₂, that react.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Each alkene molecule reacts with one Br₂ molecule. Calculate the relative molecular mass of the alkene.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Deduce the molecular formula of the alkene. Show your working.
parts.answer: C₅H₁₀

parts.label: d
parts.text: Write the structural formula of one alkene with this molecular formula, and name it.
parts.answer: CH₂=CHCH₂CH₂CH₃, pent-1-ene (or CH₃CH=CHCH₂CH₃, pent-2-ene)

practice.stem: [Mr: C₆H₁₂ = 84; C₆H₁₄ = 86. One mole of gas occupies 24 dm³ at r.t.p.]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction of hex-1-ene, C₆H₁₂, with hydrogen.
parts.answer: C₆H₁₂ + H₂ → C₆H₁₄

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the volume of hydrogen, in dm³ at r.t.p., needed to react with 4.2 g of hex-1-ene.
parts.answer: 1.2 dm³

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the mass of hexane formed.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Name the catalyst used.
parts.answer: nickel

practice.stem:
A hydrocarbon Y contains 85.7 % carbon and 14.3 % hydrogen by mass.
[Ar: H, 1; C, 12]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the empirical formula of Y. Show your working.
parts.answer: CH₂

parts.label: b
parts.text: The relative molecular mass of Y is 42. Deduce its molecular formula.
parts.answer: C₃H₆

parts.label: c
parts.text: Y decolourises aqueous bromine. Name Y and give its structural formula.
parts.answer: propene, CH₂=CHCH₃

parts.label: d
parts.text: Name the product of the reaction of Y with aqueous bromine (treat it as reaction with Br₂).
parts.answer: 1,2-dibromopropane

practice.stem: Petroleum (crude oil) is processed at refineries such as those near Karachi.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the process used to separate petroleum into fractions and state the physical property on which it depends.
parts.answer: Fractional distillation; boiling point.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one use for each fraction: (i) refinery gas (ii) kerosene (iii) bitumen.
parts.answer: (i) fuel for heating and cooking (ii) jet fuel (iii) surfacing roads and roofs

parts.label: c
parts.text: Describe how chain length and viscosity change from the top of the column to the bottom.
parts.answer: Both increase towards the bottom.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the three main fossil fuels.
parts.answer: coal, natural gas, petroleum (crude oil)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name the main constituent of natural gas.
parts.answer: methane

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Arrange these fractions in order of increasing boiling range:
bitumen, kerosene, refinery gas, diesel oil, gasoline
parts.answer: refinery gas, gasoline, kerosene, diesel oil, bitumen
parts.working: B2 all correct; B1 one pair swapped.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Which of these fractions is collected at the top of the column?
parts.answer: refinery gas

parts.label: c
parts.text: Which of these fractions is the most viscous?
parts.answer: bitumen

parts.label: d
parts.text: Give one use of bitumen.
parts.answer: making roads / roofing

practice.stem: Natural gas from fields such as Sui in Balochistan is piped to homes across Pakistan for cooking and heating.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a balanced equation for the complete combustion of methane.
parts.answer: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one reason why natural gas is a cleaner fuel than coal.
parts.answer: It produces almost no sulfur dioxide or particulates (soot) / less CO₂ per unit of energy.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why petroleum is described as a non-renewable (finite) resource.
parts.answer: It took millions of years to form and cannot be replaced once used.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give two ways in which people can help conserve petroleum.
parts.answer: Any two: use public transport/car-share; recycle plastics; use renewable energy (solar/wind); use fuel-efficient vehicles.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the conditions used for cracking.
parts.answer: high temperature; a catalyst

parts.label: b
parts.text: Complete the equation: C₁₀H₂₂ → C₇H₁₆ + ____. Name the product you have added.
parts.answer: C₃H₆; propene

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give two reasons why cracking is carried out.
parts.answer: Demand for shorter-chain fractions such as petrol is greater than supply; it produces alkenes for making polymers and other chemicals; it can produce hydrogen.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe how petroleum is separated into fractions in a fractionating column.
parts.answer: Petroleum is heated so it vaporises; vapour enters the column, which is hot at the bottom and cooler at the top; vapours rise and condense at different heights where the temperature falls below their boiling points; fractions are tapped off at different levels.
parts.working: 1 mark each for any four of: heated/vaporised; temperature gradient; vapours rise; condense when temperature below boiling point; collected at different heights.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why each fraction is a mixture and not a single compound.
parts.answer: Each fraction contains hydrocarbons with a range of similar boiling points (chain lengths).

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Describe how each property changes from the top of the fractionating column to the bottom:
(i) chain length of molecules
(ii) boiling point
(iii) viscosity
parts.answer: (i) increases (ii) increases (iii) increases

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why gasoline catches fire more easily than fuel oil.
parts.answer: Gasoline has smaller molecules / is more volatile (lower boiling point), so it vaporises and ignites more easily.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Cracking C₁₀H₂₂ gives C₅H₁₂ and one other hydrocarbon, which is an alkene. Deduce the molecular formula of the alkene and name it.
parts.answer: C₅H₁₀; pentene (pent-1-ene or pent-2-ene)
parts.working: B1 formula: C 10 − 5 = 5 and H 22 − 12 = 10; B1 name pentene (accept pent-1-ene or pent-2-ene).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write a balanced equation for the cracking of dodecane, C₁₂H₂₆, into decane and ethene.
parts.answer: C₁₂H₂₆ → C₁₀H₂₂ + C₂H₄

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the type of hydrocarbon that is always produced by cracking.
parts.answer: an alkene

practice.stem: Liquid paraffin soaked into mineral wool is heated at one end of a boiling tube. Small lumps of aluminium oxide in the middle of the tube are heated strongly so the vapour passes over them. The gas is collected over water in test-tubes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the purpose of the aluminium oxide.
parts.answer: catalyst

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the delivery tube must be removed from the water before heating stops.
parts.answer: To prevent suck-back of cold water into the hot tube (which could crack it).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the first few test-tubes of gas are thrown away.
parts.answer: They contain mainly air displaced from the apparatus.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Describe a test to show that the gas collected contains an alkene, giving the result.
parts.answer: Shake with aqueous bromine; it turns from orange to colourless.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give two environmental advantages of using natural gas instead of coal in a power station.
parts.answer: Any two: less sulfur dioxide (less acid rain); fewer particulates; less carbon dioxide per unit of energy; no ash.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one reason why a country might still burn coal.
parts.answer: Large local coal reserves (e.g. Thar coalfield) / cheaper / gas supplies running out.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name one pollutant formed from both fuels in the hot furnace, and explain how it forms.
parts.answer: Oxides of nitrogen; nitrogen and oxygen from the air react at the high temperature.

practice.stem:
Percentage supply from distillation and percentage demand for petroleum fractions at one refinery:
fraction: supply %, demand %
refinery gas: 4, 8
gasoline: 11, 22
naphtha: 9, 5
kerosene: 13, 8
diesel oil: 20, 23
fuel oil and bitumen: 43, 34

parts.label: a
parts.text: Which fractions are produced in greater amounts than are needed?
parts.answer: naphtha, kerosene, fuel oil and bitumen
parts.working: 2 marks for all four; 1 mark for two or three.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the shortfall of gasoline as a percentage of the total.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain how cracking helps to match supply with demand.
parts.answer: Cracking breaks long-chain molecules from surplus fractions (e.g. fuel oil) into shorter, more useful ones such as gasoline.

parts.label: d
parts.text: A long-chain alkane C₁₆H₃₄ is cracked to give one molecule of octane and ethene only. Write the balanced equation.
parts.answer: C₁₆H₃₄ → C₈H₁₈ + 4C₂H₄

practice.stem: [Ar: H, 1; C, 12. 1 tonne = 10⁶ g]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Complete the equation by giving the formula of the missing product: C₁₆H₃₄ → C₈H₁₈ + 2C₂H₄ + ____
parts.answer: C₄H₈

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the relative molecular mass of C₁₆H₃₄.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the maximum mass of ethene, in kg, formed from 1.00 tonne of C₁₆H₃₄ by this reaction. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
parts.answer: 248 kg

parts.label: d
parts.text: Explain why cracking is needed to match supply with demand.
parts.answer: Distillation gives more long-chain fractions than are needed and too little short-chain fuel (petrol) and alkenes; cracking converts the surplus long chains into these.
parts.working: B1 surplus of long chains; B1 converts to more useful short chains/alkenes.

practice.stem:
In an experiment, 3.55 g of decane, C₁₀H₂₂, is cracked. 480 cm³ of ethene is collected at r.t.p.
[Mr: C₁₀H₂₂ = 142. One mole of gas occupies 24 000 cm³ at r.t.p.]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of decane used.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of ethene collected.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Assuming each decane molecule that cracks gives one ethene molecule (C₁₀H₂₂ → C₈H₁₈ + C₂H₄), calculate the percentage of decane cracked.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Suggest one reason why the actual percentage of decane that reacts may be different from this value.
parts.answer: Some molecules crack in other ways (giving different products) / some ethene escapes or dissolves.

practice.stem:
Fractions from a refinery:
fraction | carbon atoms per molecule | boiling range / °C
A | 1–4 | below 25
B | 5–10 | 40–175
C | 10–16 | 175–250
D | 14–20 | 250–350
E | 20–50 | above 350

parts.label: a
parts.text: Which fraction contains dodecane, C₁₂H₂₆? Give a reason.
parts.answer: Fraction C; it has 12 carbon atoms, within the C₁₀–C₁₆ range.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the boiling point ranges increase from fraction A to fraction E.
parts.answer: Molecules are larger/longer down the list, so the intermolecular forces are stronger and more energy is needed to boil them.
parts.working: B1 larger molecules; B1 stronger intermolecular forces.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest why there is some overlap between the carbon-number ranges of fractions C and D.
parts.answer: Fractions are not perfectly separated, and molecules with the same number of carbon atoms can be branched or straight chain, so their boiling ranges overlap.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Which fraction would be cracked to produce extra gasoline? Explain.
parts.answer: Fraction D or E (heavier fractions); they contain long-chain molecules that are in surplus and can be broken into shorter ones.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Alkanes are described as saturated hydrocarbons. Explain what saturated and hydrocarbon mean.
parts.answer: Saturated: contains only single covalent bonds (C–C). Hydrocarbon: a compound of hydrogen and carbon only.

parts.label: b
parts.text: LPG cylinders used for cooking contain propane. Write a balanced equation for the complete combustion of propane, C₃H₈.
parts.answer: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O

parts.label: c
parts.text: Alkanes are generally unreactive. Give one type of reaction that they do undergo.
parts.answer: Combustion / substitution with chlorine in UV light.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the first five alkanes in order.
parts.answer: methane, ethane, propane, butane, pentane

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the molecular formula of hexane.
parts.answer: C₆H₁₄

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the type of bonds present in alkane molecules.
parts.answer: single covalent bonds only (C–C and C–H)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a balanced equation for the complete combustion of pentane, C₅H₁₂.
parts.answer: C₅H₁₂ + 8O₂ → 5CO₂ + 6H₂O

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why alkanes are used as fuels.
parts.answer: They burn releasing a lot of energy (combustion is exothermic).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a balanced equation for the incomplete combustion of methane to form carbon monoxide and water.
parts.answer: 2CH₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO + 4H₂O

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why gas water heaters (geysers) should be installed where there is good ventilation.
parts.answer: Without enough air, combustion is incomplete and carbon monoxide is produced; CO is toxic (and colourless/odourless, so not noticed).
parts.working: B1 incomplete combustion; B1 CO toxic.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the solid that may form when combustion is very incomplete.
parts.answer: carbon (soot)

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Name an alkane found in each fuel:
(i) natural gas
(ii) LPG (cooking gas cylinders)
(iii) petrol
parts.answer: (i) methane (ii) propane or butane (iii) octane (accept other C₅–C₁₀ alkanes)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain the meaning of hydrocarbon.
parts.answer: A compound containing hydrogen and carbon only.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Methane reacts with chlorine. State the condition needed.
parts.answer: ultraviolet (UV) light

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction that forms one organic product with one chlorine atom, and name that product.
parts.answer: CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl; chloromethane

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the type of reaction and explain the name.
parts.answer: Substitution: a hydrogen atom in methane is replaced by a chlorine atom.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Suggest the formula of the organic product formed if the reaction continues with more chlorine.
parts.answer: CH₂Cl₂ (or CHCl₃ / CCl₄)

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the condition needed for ethane to react with chlorine.
parts.answer: ultraviolet light (sunlight)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the equation for the reaction that forms chloroethane.
parts.answer: C₂H₆ + Cl₂ → C₂H₅Cl + HCl

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the type of reaction.
parts.answer: substitution (photochemical)

parts.label: d
parts.text: Further substitution can produce C₂H₄Cl₂. Give the structural formulae of the two isomers with this formula.
parts.answer: CH₃CHCl₂ and CH₂ClCH₂Cl

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why hexane does not decolourise aqueous bromine in the dark.
parts.answer: Hexane is saturated (no C=C), so no addition reaction can take place.

parts.label: b
parts.text: In bright sunlight, hexane slowly decolourises bromine. Name the type of reaction and one product.
parts.answer: substitution; hydrogen bromide (or a bromohexane, C₆H₁₃Br)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest why this makes bromine water an unreliable test for unsaturation if the test is done in strong sunlight.
parts.answer: Alkanes might also slowly decolourise it, giving a false positive result.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the relative molecular mass of octane, C₈H₁₈.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the percentage by mass of carbon in octane, to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write the empirical formula of octane.
parts.answer: C₄H₉

practice.stem:
LPG cylinders used for cooking contain mainly propane.
C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O
[Mr: C₃H₈ = 44; CO₂ = 44]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the mass of carbon dioxide, in kg, produced when 1.00 kg of propane burns completely. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the mass of carbon dioxide is greater than the mass of propane burned.
parts.answer: Oxygen from the air combines with the carbon (and hydrogen), adding mass.

practice.stem: [Mr: C₆H₁₄ = 86; C₆H₁₂ = 84; Ar: C, 12]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the percentage by mass of carbon in hexane, C₆H₁₄, and in hexene, C₆H₁₂. Give your answers to 3 significant figures.
parts.answer: hexane 83.7 %; hexene 85.7 %

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use your answers to suggest why hexene burns with a smokier flame than hexane.
parts.answer: Hexene has a higher proportion of carbon, so more carbon is left unburned as soot (incomplete combustion).
parts.working: B1 higher % C; B1 soot/incomplete combustion.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Butane burns completely: 2C₄H₁₀ + 13O₂ → 8CO₂ + 10H₂O. Calculate the volume of oxygen needed to burn 30 cm³ of butane, and the volume of carbon dioxide formed. (All volumes at room temperature and pressure.)
parts.answer: oxygen 195 cm³; carbon dioxide 120 cm³

parts.label: b
parts.text: In a poorly ventilated room butane burns incompletely. Name the toxic gas formed and explain why it is dangerous.
parts.answer: Carbon monoxide; it combines with haemoglobin in the blood, reducing the blood's ability to carry oxygen.

practice.stem:
20 cm³ of propane is mixed with 150 cm³ of oxygen and burned completely. The products are cooled to r.t.p.
C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the volume of oxygen used.
parts.answer: 100 cm³

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the total volume of gas left at the end, at r.t.p.
parts.answer: 110 cm³
parts.working: M1 O₂ left 150 − 100 = 50 cm³ and CO₂ formed 3 × 20 = 60 cm³; A1 50 + 60 = 110 cm³ (water is liquid at r.t.p.).

parts.label: c
parts.text: The remaining gas is shaken with aqueous sodium hydroxide. State the final volume and name the gas left.
parts.answer: 50 cm³; oxygen

practice.stem: 10 cm³ of a gaseous alkane is burned completely in excess oxygen. 40 cm³ of carbon dioxide is formed. All volumes are measured at r.t.p.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Deduce the number of carbon atoms in one molecule of the alkane. Explain.
parts.answer: 4; 10 cm³ gives 40 cm³ CO₂, so each molecule gives 4 CO₂ molecules (equal volumes contain equal numbers of molecules).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the molecular formula and name of the alkane.
parts.answer: C₄H₁₀, butane

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the volume of oxygen needed to burn the 10 cm³ completely.
parts.answer: 65 cm³
parts.working: M1 2C₄H₁₀ + 13O₂ → 8CO₂ + 10H₂O, so 6.5 volumes O₂ per volume; A1 65 cm³.

practice.stem:
An alkane Z contains 82.8 % carbon and 17.2 % hydrogen by mass.
[Ar: H, 1; C, 12]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the empirical formula of Z. Show your working.
parts.answer: C₂H₅

parts.label: b
parts.text: The relative molecular mass of Z is 58. Deduce the molecular formula of Z.
parts.answer: C₄H₁₀

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give the structural formulae of the two isomers of Z.
parts.answer: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ and CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₃

parts.label: a
parts.text:
How many moles of sodium hydroxide are in 25.0 cm³ of 0.200 mol/dm³ aqueous sodium hydroxide?
A 0.00500
B 0.0500
C 5.00
D 8.00
parts.working: moles = 0.200 × 25.0/1000 = 0.00500 mol. C forgets to convert cm³ to dm³.

practice.stem:
25.0 cm³ of aqueous sodium hydroxide is exactly neutralised by 20.00 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid.
NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of hydrochloric acid used.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the concentration of the sodium hydroxide in mol/dm³.
parts.answer: 0.0800 mol/dm³

parts.label: a
parts.text:
What volume of 0.250 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid contains 0.0100 mol of HCl?
A 2.50 cm³
B 25.0 cm³
C 40.0 cm³
D 400 cm³
parts.answer: C 40.0 cm³
parts.working: volume = moles ÷ concentration = 0.0100 ÷ 0.250 = 0.0400 dm³ = 40.0 cm³. D (400 cm³) comes from converting dm³ to cm³ wrongly; A comes from multiplying 0.0100 × 0.250 × 1000.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A technician in a school laboratory in Multan dissolves 5.85 g of sodium chloride in water and makes the solution up to 250 cm³. Calculate the concentration of the solution in g/dm³.
parts.answer: 23.4 g/dm³

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the concentration of this solution in mol/dm³. [Mr: NaCl, 58.5]
parts.answer: 0.400 mol/dm³

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the mass of anhydrous sodium carbonate, Na₂CO₃, needed to make 500 cm³ of a 0.200 mol/dm³ solution. [Mr: Na₂CO₃, 106]

practice.stem:
A student titrates 25.0 cm³ portions of aqueous potassium hydroxide with 0.150 mol/dm³ nitric acid, using methyl orange.
KOH + HNO₃ → KNO₃ + H₂O
Titration: 1 (rough), 2, 3, 4
Titre / cm³: 21.40, 20.85, 20.95, 20.90

parts.label: a
parts.text: Which titres are concordant? Calculate the mean titre to use.
parts.answer: Titrations 2, 3 and 4 (20.85, 20.95, 20.90 cm³); mean = 20.90 cm³
parts.working: B1 choosing the three results within 0.10 cm³ of each other (not the rough titre); B1 mean 20.90 cm³

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of nitric acid in the mean titre.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the concentration of the potassium hydroxide in mol/dm³. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
parts.answer: 0.125 mol/dm³

parts.label: a
parts.text:
What is the concentration, in g/dm³, of 0.150 mol/dm³ aqueous sodium hydroxide? [Mr: NaOH, 40]
A 0.00375 g/dm³
B 3.75 g/dm³
C 6.00 g/dm³
D 267 g/dm³
parts.answer: C 6.00 g/dm³
parts.working: g/dm³ = mol/dm³ × Mr = 0.150 × 40 = 6.00. B divides by 40 instead of multiplying.

practice.stem:
25.0 cm³ of 0.120 mol/dm³ aqueous sodium hydroxide is neutralised by 18.75 cm³ of dilute sulfuric acid.
2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of sodium hydroxide in 25.0 cm³.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the concentration of the sulfuric acid in mol/dm³.
parts.answer: 0.0800 mol/dm³

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the concentration of the sulfuric acid in g/dm³. [Mr: H₂SO₄, 98]
parts.answer: 7.84 g/dm³

practice.stem:
A student dilutes 25.0 cm³ of a brand of vinegar to 250 cm³ with distilled water. 25.0 cm³ of the diluted vinegar needs 21.60 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ aqueous sodium hydroxide for neutralisation.
CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the concentration of ethanoic acid in the diluted vinegar.
parts.answer: 0.0864 mol/dm³

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the concentration of ethanoic acid in the original vinegar in mol/dm³ and in g/dm³. [Mr: CH₃COOH, 60]
parts.answer: 0.864 mol/dm³; 51.8 g/dm³

parts.label: a
parts.text:
20.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ sulfuric acid exactly neutralises 25.0 cm³ of aqueous potassium hydroxide.
2KOH + H₂SO₄ → K₂SO₄ + 2H₂O
What is the concentration of the potassium hydroxide?
A 0.0800 mol/dm³
B 0.125 mol/dm³
C 0.160 mol/dm³
D 0.200 mol/dm³
parts.answer: C 0.160 mol/dm³
parts.working: moles H₂SO₄ = 0.100 × 0.0200 = 0.00200; moles KOH = 2 × 0.00200 = 0.00400; concentration = 0.00400 ÷ 0.0250 = 0.160 mol/dm³. A (0.0800) ignores the 2 : 1 mole ratio.

practice.stem: A laboratory assistant in Karachi dilutes 50.0 cm³ of 2.00 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid with distilled water to a total volume of 400 cm³.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the concentration of the diluted acid.
parts.answer: 0.250 mol/dm³

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Calculate the volume of the diluted acid needed to react exactly with 1.06 g of anhydrous sodium carbonate.
Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂   [Mr: Na₂CO₃, 106]
parts.answer: 80.0 cm³

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the piece of apparatus that should be used to measure the 50.0 cm³ of the original acid accurately.
parts.answer: pipette
parts.working: B1 pipette (fixed volume, accurate); a measuring cylinder is not accurate enough

practice.stem:
Limewater is a solution of calcium hydroxide. 25.0 cm³ of limewater is titrated with 0.0500 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid. 18.40 cm³ of acid is needed.
Ca(OH)₂ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + 2H₂O

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of hydrochloric acid used.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the concentration of calcium hydroxide in the limewater in mol/dm³.
parts.answer: 0.0184 mol/dm³

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the concentration in g/dm³. Give your answer to 3 significant figures. [Mr: Ca(OH)₂, 74]
parts.answer: 1.36 g/dm³

practice.stem:
An antacid tablet of mass 0.500 g contains calcium carbonate. It is added to 50.0 cm³ of 0.500 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid (an excess). When the reaction stops, the excess acid in the whole solution is titrated and needs 64.00 cm³ of 0.250 mol/dm³ aqueous sodium hydroxide.
CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂;  NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O   [Mr: CaCO₃, 100]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of hydrochloric acid added at the start.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of hydrochloric acid left over (in excess).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the mass of calcium carbonate in the tablet.
parts.working: acid reacted = 0.0090 mol M1; CaCO₃ = 0.0045 mol × 100 = 0.450 g A1

parts.label: d
parts.text: Calculate the percentage by mass of calcium carbonate in the tablet.

practice.stem:
1.40 g of the hydroxide of a Group I metal, MOH, is dissolved in water and made up to 250 cm³ in a volumetric flask. 25.0 cm³ of this solution is neutralised by 25.00 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid.
MOH + HCl → MCl + H₂O   [Ar: H, 1; O, 16]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of MOH in 25.0 cm³ of the solution and in the 250 cm³ flask.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the relative formula mass of MOH.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Deduce the relative atomic mass of M and identify M.
parts.answer: 39; potassium

practice.stem:
A student wants to find the number of molecules of water of crystallisation in a sample of washing soda crystals, Na₂CO₃·xH₂O, without heating them. 3.58 g of the crystals are dissolved in water and made up to 250 cm³ in a volumetric flask. 25.0 cm³ of this solution needs 25.00 cm³ of 0.100 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid for neutralisation.
Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of hydrochloric acid in the titre.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of Na₂CO₃ in 25.0 cm³ of solution and in the whole 250 cm³.
parts.answer: 0.00125 mol in 25.0 cm³; 0.0125 mol in 250 cm³

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the relative formula mass of the hydrated crystals, Na₂CO₃·xH₂O.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Deduce the value of x. [Ar: H, 1; C, 12; O, 16; Na, 23]

practice.stem:
30.0 cm³ of 0.200 mol/dm³ aqueous sodium hydroxide is mixed with 20.0 cm³ of 0.250 mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid. Assume the volumes simply add.
NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of sodium hydroxide and of hydrochloric acid mixed.
parts.answer: NaOH 0.00600 mol; HCl 0.00500 mol

parts.label: b
parts.text: State which reactant is in excess and whether the final solution is acidic, neutral or alkaline.
parts.answer: sodium hydroxide is in excess; the solution is alkaline
parts.working: 1 : 1 ratio, 0.00600 > 0.00500 so NaOH left over → alkaline

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the concentration of hydroxide ions left in the mixture, in mol/dm³.
parts.answer: 0.0200 mol/dm³
parts.working: excess = 0.00100 mol (M1); total volume 50.0 cm³ so 0.00100 ÷ 0.0500 = 0.0200 mol/dm³ (A1)

parts.label: d
parts.text: Calculate the concentration of sodium chloride in the mixture, in mol/dm³.
parts.answer: 0.100 mol/dm³

parts.label: a
parts.text:
How many moles of carbon dioxide molecules are in 4.4 g of carbon dioxide? [Mr: CO₂, 44]
A 0.010
B 0.10
C 1.0
D 10
parts.working: moles = mass ÷ Mr = 4.4 ÷ 44 = 0.10 mol. A is a factor of 10 too small.

practice.stem:
In a lime kiln in Sindh, limestone (calcium carbonate) is heated strongly.
CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂   [Ar: C, 12; O, 16; Ca, 40]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of calcium carbonate in 25.0 g.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the mass of calcium oxide formed when 25.0 g of calcium carbonate is completely decomposed.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State one use of calcium oxide.
parts.answer: Neutralising acidic soil (or making cement / removing acidic gases)

parts.label: a
parts.text:
What mass of sodium hydroxide reacts exactly with 0.50 mol of sulfuric acid?
2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O   [Mr: NaOH, 40]
A 20 g
B 40 g
C 49 g
D 80 g
parts.answer: B 40 g
parts.working: moles NaOH = 2 × 0.50 = 1.0 mol; mass = 1.0 × 40 = 40 g. A (20 g) uses a 1 : 1 ratio; C (49 g) is the mass of the acid.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of atoms in 0.50 mol of magnesium. [Avogadro constant = 6.02 × 10²³ /mol]
parts.answer: 3.01 × 10²³ atoms

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of oxygen molecules, O₂, in 3.2 g of oxygen. [Ar: O, 16]
parts.answer: 0.10 mol

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the number of oxygen molecules and the number of oxygen atoms in 3.2 g of oxygen.
parts.answer: 6.02 × 10²² molecules; 1.204 × 10²³ (1.20 × 10²³) atoms
parts.working: 0.10 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 6.02 × 10²² molecules (B1); each molecule has 2 atoms so 1.20 × 10²³ atoms (B1)

practice.stem:
Railway workers weld steel rails together using the thermite reaction. Aluminium powder reacts with iron(III) oxide and produces molten iron.
Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe   [Ar: O, 16; Al, 27; Fe, 56]

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the number of moles of aluminium in 5.4 g.
parts.answer: 0.20 mol

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the mass of iron formed from 5.4 g of aluminium.
parts.working: 1 : 1 ratio Al : Fe so 0.20 mol Fe (M1); 0.20 × 56 = 11.2 g (A1)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the mass of iron(III) oxide that reacts with 5.4 g of aluminium.

practice.stem:
Charcoal is burned in a barbecue grill at a family gathering in Islamabad.
C + O₂ → CO₂   [Ar: C, 12; O, 16]

parts.label: a
